input: We propose a technique for embedding imperceptible multi-bit text watermarks using paraphrasing with Language Models (LLMs). A pair of paraphrasers is fine-tuned which behave differently from each other. Their paraphrasing differences, which are subtle, can be detected by a trained decoder due to variations in text semantics. We use a text classifier as our decoder system to decode the multi-bit watermark after applying alternative paraphrasers on predefined sentence level data. Experimental results demonstrate that our watermarks can achieve a detection AUC of over 99.99% even with small (1.1B) paraphrasing models, while the original sentence's semantic content remains intact. An additional benefit is the robustness of our method in resisting word substitutions, sentence-level paraphrases etc. , as well as generalizing effectively to new data. The stealthiness of the watermark is also confirmed by LLM-based evaluations. We released the code online for further research here: this https URL

sentences: We propose an imperceptible multi-bit text watermark embedded by paraphrasing with large language models (LLMs).
We fine-tune a pair of LLM paraphraseers that behave differently to reflect their differences in the text semantics.
To embed our multi-bit watermark, we encode pre-defined binary codes at the sentence level using two paraphraseers alternately.
Then, we use a text classifier as the decoder to decode each bit of the watermark.
Through extensive experiments, we show that our watermarks achieve over 99.99\% detection AUC with small (1.1B) text paraphrases while preserving the semantic information of the original sentence.
More importantly, our pipeline is robust under word substitution and sentence paraphrasing perturbations and generalizes well to out-of-distributional data.
